s0: Calgary, with the Rocky Mountains on its doorstep.
How far could tourism here really go?
s1: In twenty twenty-five, Calgary welcomed ten and a half million visitors.
They spent three point three billion dollars.
Hotels were sixty-seven and a half percent full.
And tourism and hospitality supported eighty-four thousand jobs.
s2: Where does that money come from? Two dollars in every three are spent by Canadians.
One in three comes from visitors from the United States and overseas.
And that share is growing. In the first quarter of twenty twenty-six, international visitor spending rose more than fifteen percent.
s3: Calgary's airport handled nineteen point four million passengers in twenty twenty-five, flying non-stop to one hundred and ten destinations.
Fifteen new routes were added in one year. And twenty twenty-six brought the first non-stops to South America and the Middle East.
s4: More than seven million international travellers connect through Calgary every year, and never leave the airport.
If just one percent of them stayed, that would be seventy thousand more visitors.
It has started. Since June twenty twenty-six, a stopover program lets travellers on two WestJet routes from the United Kingdom spend up to seven days in Calgary, at no extra airfare.
s5: Calgary is also a base camp.
Banff National Park just had a record four and a half million visitors, and Calgary is its nearest international airport.
Five UNESCO World Heritage Sites lie within a few hours' drive.
s6: And the city already draws a crowd.
The Calgary Stampede generated seven hundred and twenty-one million dollars across Alberta in twenty twenty-five.
Meetings and conventions brought two hundred and forty million dollars.
Sport, culture and major events added nearly one hundred and twenty-three million more.
s7: Other places have turned passing traffic into tourism.
Iceland offered a free stopover, and its visitor numbers roughly tripled in six years.
Singapore's free city tour for transit passengers drew more than eighty thousand people in twenty nineteen.
Denver measured two hundred and nineteen dollars in visitor spending for every dollar of advertising.
And Dubai, with festivals all year round, fills almost eighty-one percent of its hotel rooms.
s8: Tourism Calgary's goal: double visitor spending, to six billion dollars, by twenty thirty-five.
That means about six percent growth, every year.
Growth has costs too: crowding in Banff, and housing pressure from short-term rentals.
s9: The room to grow is international.
